title: Molly Malone
content:
In {C}Dublin's fair {a}city where the {d}girls are so {G7}pretty 
I {C}first set my {a}eyes on sweet {d}Molly Ma{G7}lone.
Where she {C}wheeled her wheel{a}barrow through {d}streets broad and {G7}narrow,
crying: "{C}Cockles and {a}mussels, a{C}live, a{G7}live {C}oh"
"A{C}live, alive {a}oh, a{d}live, alive {G7}oh", crying: "{C}Cockles and {a}mussels, {C}alive, a{G7}live {C}oh"

She was a fishmonger and sure 'twas no wonder.
For so were her father and mother before.
And they both wheeled their barrows through ...

She died of a fever and no one could save her
and that was the end of sweet Molly Malone.
But her ghost wheels her barrow through ...
